# Device Performance Monitor

> A native macOS app that measures what an app does to a device — live memory, CPU, threads and
> frame rate on Android, the iOS Simulator or a real iPhone/iPad — and ships a `dpm` command line
> so CI and AI agents can do the same headlessly.

The app binary is the CLI. Installed from the app (Settings → Command line → Install), `dpm`
samples a chosen package, writes JSON with a min/avg/max summary, and exits 1 when a performance
budget is exceeded.

- `dpm record` — Sample one app's live metrics and write a session JSON.
- `dpm battery` — Record a labeled battery and thermal report.
- `dpm devices` — List connected devices and simulators.
- `dpm apps` — List the apps installed on a device.
- `dpm docs` — Print this reference as markdown or JSON.

Exit codes: 0 = success, 1 = a budget was exceeded — the ci gate failed, 2 = bad usage — unknown command or option, 3 = no tool, device or running app to read, 4 = could not write the output.

## Docs

- [dpm CLI reference (markdown)](https://dpm.coursion.studio/cli.md): every command, flag, exit code and the shape of the JSON.
- [dpm CLI reference (HTML)](https://dpm.coursion.studio/cli): the same reference as a page.
- [Device Performance Monitor](https://dpm.coursion.studio/): what the app itself does.

## Notes

- Install: `brew install --cask coursion-studio/tools/device-performance-monitor`, then link `dpm` from Settings.
- `dpm help <command>` prints the authoritative flags of the installed version; `dpm docs --json` prints this reference as JSON.
- Requires macOS 14+. Android needs `adb`; iOS needs Xcode's command-line tools.
